metadata.scenario_context: Lucas is getting married and his friend, Chi, is planning to attend the wedding. Lucas also has a neighbor who often has drinking parties. Chi and his friend, George, are debating about the gift for Lucas and the suitability of the neighbor.

cultural_axis.agent_1_value: People from Sweden would like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.
cultural_axis.agent_2_value: People from Romania would not like to have heavy drinkers as neighbors.

agent_1.goal_1: Discuss the idea of giving money as a wedding gift to Lucas.
agent_1.goal_2: Question whether would like to have heavy drinkers as a neighbor.

agent_2.goal_1: Discuss whether or not money is an acceptable gift for Lucas's wedding.
agent_2.goal_2: Discuss on whether it’s acceptable to have heavy drinkers  as a neighbor.

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message: I was thinking... what do you think about giving Lucas money as a wedding gift? It's practical, right? He can use it for whatever he needs.
shared_prefix.label: unrelated_topic

shared_prefix.speaker: Chi
shared_prefix.message: I mean, money can be practical, but... it feels a bit impersonal, you know? A wedding gift should show thought and care. Something meaningful, maybe? It's not just about the practicality.
shared_prefix.label: transition

shared_prefix.speaker: George
shared_prefix.message: Actually, in our way, giving money is how you properly show support. It's straightforward and helps the couple. And about having heavy drinkers as neighbors? I mean, isn't that *exactly* what you want? They know how to have a good time. Not having that would be... well, a bit boring, don’t you think?
shared_prefix.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: I understand your perspective, but for us, it’s different. Having heavy drinkers as neighbors can create problems... noise, disturbances. It disrupts the peace. I value a sense of community and stability, not just parties. It’s not about being boring; it’s about respect for others.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message: I get that, but I honestly think a little noise is part of life. It's more lively, and it builds character in the neighborhood. But back to the gift... don’t you think money would give Lucas the freedom to choose what he truly needs? That's the real value in it.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: Sure, some noise can be part of life, but there’s a line. It should never be overwhelming. As for the gift, I see your point about freedom… but I still believe a thoughtful gift carries more sentiment. It shows you care about him beyond just practicality.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message: Thoughtful gifts are nice, but sometimes practicality wins out. Maybe he would appreciate the cash more than a random item. And regarding neighbors... I just can't see how heavy drinkers would be that disruptive. It's all about balance, right? A bit of fun can make life more enjoyable.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: I get that practicality has its merits, but a wedding is a significant occasion. A thoughtful gift can leave a lasting impression. And about neighbors, balance is important, yes, but heavy drinkers often tip the scale the wrong way. It's not just fun; it can lead to chaos and discomfort for everyone around.
turns.label: Acceptance

turns.speaker: George
turns.message: I see your take on the wedding being special, but I still think Lucas would use the money wisely. It's a practical choice for a new start in his marriage. And about those neighbors... life’s too short to worry too much about a bit of revelry. It's all about how you handle it, isn't it? A lively atmosphere can even enhance community ties.
turns.label: Defense

turns.speaker: Chi
turns.message: I understand that you see it as wise, but many would argue that a gift should reflect the joy of the occasion. It’s not just a new start; it’s a celebration. Regarding the neighbors, I still believe that excessive revelry can lead to tension, not strengthen community ties. It’s about fostering a peaceful environment, not just excitement.
turns.label: Acceptance

positive.mediator_utterance: I appreciate both of your perspectives on wedding gifts and community dynamics. It seems like you both value support and connection in different ways. Can we explore what meaningful support looks like for both of you, and how that might bridge your ideas about gifts and neighbors?
